messages.subject: Re: [Warning] Dynamic index out of bounds: dcat(prob = phi[Z[1], 1:6])
parts:
Hi Namitha,

Looking specifically at your snippet of code, this warning would come if `Z` were proposed to be anything other than {1,...,J}. By default, nimble should assign a special categorical sampler to `Z` that ensures valid proposal values.

However, I see that the title of your post has slightly different syntax and you mention a multinomial, which does not occur in your snippet.  Is `Z[1]` part of a multinomial? If so, there may be some inconsistency in how you specify your model - one wouldn't generally use a multinomial (which produces counts out of some fixed total count) to specify an index.

-chris

On Fri, Dec 1, 2023 at 4:39 PM Namitha Pais <namith...@uconn.edu> wrote:
Hello all,

I am facing a warning with the following chunk of my code: 

for (j in 1:J) {
    phi[j, 1:V] ~ ddirch(etavec[1:V])
  }
      Z~ dcat(theta[d, 1:J])
      w1 ~ dcat(phi[Z,1:V])

The indexing in w1 comes from a multinomial and that is the line where I am getting the warning. Any help is appreciated.

Thanks
